content: The provided text is a detailed description of drug interactions involving ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, a combination antiviral medication used to treat hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. 1. Dosage Recommendations for Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: For patients weighing 17 to <35 kg: Administer one tablet or packet containing 45 mg/200 mg orally once daily. For patients weighing ≥35 kg: Administer one tablet containing 90 mg/400 mg orally once daily, or two tablets/packets of 45 mg/200 mg orally once daily. 2. Treatment Duration: Treatment-naïve patients without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A): Standard duration is 12 weeks. An 8-week regimen may be considered for treatment-naïve patients without cirrhosis and with pre-treatment HCV RNA levels <6 million IU/mL. Treatment-experienced patients without cirrhosis: 12 weeks. Treatment-experienced patients with compensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A): 24 weeks. Adding daily weight-based ribavirin may be considered. Patients with decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B or C), including post-liver transplantation: 12 weeks in combination with ribavirin. 3. Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Testing: All patients should be tested for current or prior HBV infection before initiating treatment with HCV direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). 4. Drug Interactions: Carbamazepine, Fosphenytoin, Oxcarbazepine, Phenobarbital, Phenytoin, Rifabutin, Rifampin, Rifapentine, St. John’s Wort, Tipranavir: These drugs are contraindicated as they induce P-glycoprotein (P-gp), reducing sofosbuvir levels and its active metabolite (GS-331007), which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Colchicine: Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases colchicine levels via P-gp inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Darolutamide: Avoid coadministration due to its inhibition of breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. Edoxaban: Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases edoxaban levels via P-gp inhibition. Dose adjustment may be required. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce edoxaban dose to 30 mg once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. Enasidenib: Avoid coadministration with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. If unavoidable, reduce substrate dosage as per prescribing information. Erdafitinib: If coadministration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Lasmiditan: Avoid coadministration due to BCRP inhibition. If unavoidable, monitor closely. Leniolisib: Avoid coadministration as it increases systemic exposure of BCRP substrates. Repotrectinib: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Resmetirom: Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. Rimegepant: Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sotorasib: Avoid coadministration. If unavoidable, refer to prescribing information for dosage modifications. Tepotinib: If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. Topotecan: Avoid coadministration with oral topotecan due to P-gp inhibition. Interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. Venetoclax: Reduce venetoclax dose by at least 50% if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for signs of venetoclax toxicities. Acalabrutinib: Use caution as it may increase exposure to BCRP substrates by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Aluminum Hydroxide, Magnesium Carbonate, Magnesium Trisilicate, Calcium Carbonate, Cimetidine, Citric Acid/Sodium Bicarbonate, Dexlansoprazole, Esomeprazole: These drugs increase gastric pH, reducing ledipasvir solubility and levels. Separate administration of antacids and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by 4 hours. For H2-receptor antagonists, administer simultaneously or 12 hours apart at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg BID. Proton-pump inhibitors comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered under fasted conditions. Amiodarone: Increases risk of bradycardia, potentially fatal, when coadministered with sofosbuvir and another DAA. Monitor cardiac function inpatient for the first 48 hours, followed by outpatient or self-monitoring for at least 2 weeks. Atorvastatin: Coadministration may increase the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Monitor closely. Berotralstat: Monitor or titrate P-gp substrate dose if coadministered. Betrixaban: Reduce dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Dabigatran: Avoid coadministration with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. Danicopan: Increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Digoxin: Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. Duvelisib: Use caution and monitor closely. Elagolix: Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir levels may increase. Dose regimen alteration may be necessary. Encorafenib: Monitor for increased exposure and toxicities of BCRP substrates. Adjust dose as needed.
